CO1: Show that a fee is the gap between what a transaction's inputs hold and its outputs hold, say why only the spender's signature can commit to it, and describe what a miner chooses
CO2: Compute the virtual size and the fee rate of a transaction from its weight, convert between the units a node uses, and state the minimum rates and the dust limits a node applies
CO3: Explain how a node estimates the fee rate for a target number of blocks from the past, what it needs before it answers, and read the fee market of two mainnet blocks
CO4: State what a replacement transaction must pay, how the opt-in signal differs from full replacement, and judge the hazards that replacement brings
CO5: Work out the package fee rate that lifts a cheap parent, explain package relay and the cluster mempool, and say how a large child pins a parent and what version 3 and anchors change
CO6: Explain fee sniping and the lock time defence, and judge how much the defence matters when fees are a small or a large part of a miner's income
_serves: These six outcomes are chapter 9's: who pays a fee and what it is (CO1), how it is priced (CO2), how it is estimated (CO3), how a payment is replaced (CO4), how a cheap parent is lifted and how that can be blocked (CO5), and why the lock time matters (CO6).
